limitations: A geography match is not proof of a bilateral route between target countries.

The records are selected reported incidents, not a complete flow series or an estimate of successful movement.

economic_findings.interpretation: The current-account balance measures the national flow relative to GDP. A smaller deficit can reflect weaker imports as well as stronger export earnings.
economic_findings.text: MMR: Current account balance (% of GDP) was 0.09 percent of GDP in 2019. That compares with -3.77 in 2018 (3.86 percentage points higher).
economic_findings.title: External financing balance

evidence.unit: percent of exports and primary income
percent of exports and primary income

economic_findings.interpretation: A higher ratio means more annual export and primary-income receipts are matched by external debt service. It does not identify the creditor or a project's repayment burden.
economic_findings.text: MMR: Total debt service (% of exports of goods, services and primary income) was 7.39 percent of exports and primary income in 2024. That compares with 6.99 in 2023 (0.39 percentage points higher).
economic_findings.title: Debt service against export earnings

economic_findings.interpretation: Reserve cover provides a national external-liquidity comparison. Gross reserves do not show every encumbrance or contingent liability.
economic_findings.text: MMR: Total reserves in months of imports was 3.29 months of imports in 2019. That compares with 3.11 in 2018 (0.18 months of imports higher).
economic_findings.title: Reserve coverage of imports

economic_findings.interpretation: Lower inflation means prices rise more slowly; it does not mean the previous price increases have reversed. This national annual series does not measure local household costs.
economic_findings.text: MMR: Inflation, consumer prices (annual %) was 8.83 percent annual change in 2019. That compares with 6.87 in 2018 (1.95 percentage points higher).
